title: Performance
description: Set a measurable performance target and compare the change with a representative baseline.
expertises: Service latency, throughput and resource use
questions: Which user journey or service call needs a performance budget?
What baseline, traffic shape and dataset represent real use?
Which measurement separates client rendering, service work and upstream delays?

specialists.title: Client performance engineer
specialists.focus: Choose a user-visible interaction and measure it across the devices, browsers and network conditions that matter to the audience.

specialists.title: Service performance engineer
specialists.focus: Break down time across queueing, service work, storage and upstream calls. Identify the bottleneck that the proposal addresses.

specialists.title: Capacity engineer
specialists.focus: Compare expected concurrency and growth with measured saturation. Quantify headroom, cost and behavior when an upstream service slows.

specialists.title: Benchmark reviewer
specialists.focus: Check that baseline and candidate runs are comparable. Examine sample size, cache state and variance before interpreting an apparent improvement.

evidence: Target journey and performance budget, with metric, unit, percentile or range, and representative users or traffic.
Before-and-after measurements from the same environment and workload, with sample counts, warm-up and cache conditions, errors and timeouts.
Trace, profile or query plan that locates time spent and resource growth along the path most likely to improve.
Latency and resource use at normal and peak demand with estimated capacity margin and operating cost.
Regression gate or monitoring query, with threshold, measurement window and owner.
challenge: Did the apparent speedup come from warmer caches, a different dataset or fewer concurrent requests?
What happens to tail latency and the completion rate if the slowest dependency gets slower?
Does the improvement hold for the device, tenant or request shape with the highest cost?
Which resource reaches its limit first, and how will users notice it?
decision_criteria: Recommend the change when it meets the agreed user-facing budget on representative runs and stays within the resource limits.
Request another measurement when test conditions differ, samples are sparse or the effect is smaller than normal variance.
Prefer a targeted fix when evidence identifies the bottleneck and the simpler change meets the budget.
Hold rollout expansion if the agreed tail-latency, error or saturation limits are exceeded.
